Mason: Heads-up — got a pager for elevated p99 on hosted inference in us-west-2. Looks like a throughput drop + retries. I'm primary for this shift, leaving in ~30m, need a clean handoff if we can't stable it.
Priya: copying. what's the customer impact? any 5xx?
Mason: Mostly 503s and a few timed-out requests; token churn is spiking. Routing shows fallback to smaller model triggered a lot. 2 customers with high QPS saw errors.
IncidentBot: [pager] Alert: inference.p99_us-west-2 > 1200ms for 10m — severity: high — runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-p99
Ari: On it. Mason, can you paste the quick checklist you used? will take primary if you need to step out.
Mason: Sure — quick triage notes: 
- check serving pool health: `rbctl svc list --region us-west-2`
- check gpu util and mem: `ssh gpu-ops-01 -- nvidia-smi`
- check redis KV cache hitrate: `redis-cli INFO stats | grep keyspace_hits`
- check model fallback logs in cloudwatch: `cw tail /redwood/inference/us-west-2/fallback`
- temporary mitigation: scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes, or enable canary fallback to smaller quantized variant with 50% traffic.
Elena: If we scale, do ping ops to avoid overcommit. Also watch latency on the smaller model — quality regressions may be customer-visible.
Sam: If routing is choking, we can enable route-slicing: send premium customers to dedicated pool, everything else to burst pool. Command to toggle: `rbctl route update --region us-west-2 --route-slice premium=dedicated,default=burst`
Mason: I already tried bumping burst pool once; it helped briefly then errors came back. KV cache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 56% at the spike.
Priya: That suggests cache miss storm. Prior quick fix is to flush prefix cache for the long-tail keys: `redis-cli EVAL "return redis.call('FLUSHDB')" 0` — careful, that's global. Better: `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'kv:prefix:*' | xargs redis-cli del` (targeted).
Ari: Agree, target delete. Also check whether sequence length spiked, causing a larger KV footprint.
DeployBot: Deploy notification: `canary/fallback-quantized` rollout at 5401234590 by infra-ops (50% traffic).
Mason: That rollout may have produced more simultaneous model loads — check model load logs.
Elena: Quick mitigation playbook I'm pasting: 
1) Route premium traffic to dedicated pool (min 2 nodes)
2) Enable fallback-quantized at 25% first, monitor quality and p99
3) Throttle non-critical background requests via rate-limit rule: `rate-limiter set --route /embed --qps 20`
4) Targeted KV prefix purge for <24h keys only
5) If p99 still > 1s after 10m, scale dedicated pool by +1 and open incident bridge.
Ari: I'll take primary now, Mason you can hand off. Leaving steps for the incoming oncall: 
- open the incident bridge if we hit step 5: `incident bridge create --sev high --channel #incident-usw2`
- post an initial customer-impact note in #support-ops with counts and affected model(s)
- if you scale, set an autoscale cooldown to 5m so we don't thrash.
Mason: Handing off to Ari — I'm stepping out. Notes are in the thread and I pinned the links. :wave:
Priya: Ari — when you have a sec, can you confirm whether the fallback-quantized increased model load concurrency? check `modelmgr metric active_loads{model="gptx-8k"}`
Ari: On it. Quick findings: active_loads jumped by ~3 per host after the canary. Also saw increased cold starts in the logs (lots of model mmap). I'm toggling canary back to 10% and enabling cached mmap for the quantized variant.
Sam: If mmap helps, we should consider pinning warmed workers for the quantized variant temporarily: `rbctl pool set --warmers quantized=true --count 2`
IncidentBot: Update: severity remains high. p99 1050ms -> 890ms after partial mitigations.
Ari: Good improvement. Next steps (for whoever covers next): 
- watch p99 and KV hitrate for 30m, if hitrate < 80% run targeted prefix purge + warmers,
- prepare rollback plan for fallback-quantized if customer complaints spike: `rbctl route update --region us-west-2 --fallback disabled`
- doc link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-handoff-cheatsheet (contains the routing and KV purge snippets)
Elena: I'm adding a short postmortem checklist into the incident ticket: capture peak QPS, KV miss rate, model load counts, and rollout timestamps.
Mason: thanks team. Ari you're primary; Priya you're secondary for 2h. I'll update the handoff doc later.
Ari: Copy. I'll update #incidents with a short status in 10m.
Priya: Standing by. :mag:
Elena: +1. If anything escalates ping me directly. :phone:
